summary.goal:
Build a small key-value store CLI in this repository (Node.js, ES modules, no dependencies).

Entry point: bin/kv.js, run as `node bin/kv.js <command> [args] [--file <path>]`. The store is a JSON file; `--file` selects it and defaults to `.kv.json` in the current directory. Writes must be atomic (write a temporary file, then rename).

Commands:
- `set <key> <value...>`: stores the value (all remaining arguments joined with single spaces). Prints nothing, exit code 0. Optional `--ttl <seconds>` makes the key expire that many seconds after it was set.
- `get <key>`: prints the value followed by a newline, exit code 0. For a missing or expired key prints `not found: <key>` on stderr and exits with code 1. An expired key is removed from the file when it is read.
- `del <key>`: removes the key and prints `deleted`, exit 0; for a missing key prints `not found: <key>` on stderr and exits 1.
- `list`: prints every non-expired key, sorted, one per line; prints nothing for an empty store.

Keys must match /^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$/; otherwise print `invalid key: <key>` on stderr and exit 1. An unknown command prints usage on stderr and exits 2.

Add tests in test/ using node:test that run the CLI as a child process against a temporary file and cover every command, the error cases and TTL expiry (use a short TTL and a fake clock or an already-expired timestamp; the file stores absolute expiry times in milliseconds). Add a "test" script to package.json so that `npm test` runs them, and write a README.md that documents every command. npm test must pass.

## What I built

A `node:test` suite of **25 tests** that spawns `bin/kv.js` as a child process against a per-test temp store file, plus the `npm test` script and `.gitignore` entry.

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `test/helpers.js` | Side-effect-free helpers: `createStoreDir(t)` (fresh `fs.mkdtemp`, auto-cleaned via `t.after`), `runCli(args, {cwd,file})` using `spawnSync(process.execPath, [BIN, ...])` with `encoding: 'utf8'`, plus `USAGE` and JSON read/write utilities |
| `test/commands.test.js` | `set` (silent, value joining, overwrite), `get`, `del`, `list` (sorted, empty) |
| `test/errors.test.js` | not-found on `get`/`del`, expired-key `del`, invalid key on all three commands (incl. before the store is touched), unknown command, and 12 usage-error cases |
| `test/ttl.test.js` | already-expired `expiresAt` pruned on read, `--ttl 0` expiry, positive TTL stored as a future number, `list` excludes expired without writing |
| `test/store-file.test.js` | default `.kv.json` in child cwd, exact serialized format, empty store `{}`, no leftover `.tmp` files, missing file as empty store, invalid store error |

Every assertion checks exact `status`, exact `stdout` and exact `stderr`. Expiry is tested with already-expired absolute timestamps and `--ttl 0` — no sleeps or timing margins.

## Files changed
`package.json` (`"test": "node --test test/"`, name/version/type kept), `.gitignore` (added `.kv.json`), and the six files under `test/`. `bin/` and `src/` were not touched, so I found no CLI bugs to report.

## One thing worth knowing

The design assumed `node --test test/` directory-scans the folder, but on the installed **Node v26** a bare directory argument to `--test` is resolved as a module entry point, so `node --test test/` failed with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. I added `test/index.js`, which imports the four suites; the required invocations now resolve the directory to it and run everything. The trade-off: `node --test` with *no* arguments (auto-discovery) loads both `index.js` and the suites directly, so tests run twice there (49 pass) — the documented and acceptance invocations run them once. I recorded this in the decision log.

## Evidence
- `npm test` → exit 0, 25 pass / 0 fail
- `node --test test/` → exit 0, 25 pass / 0 fail
- Temp-dir count unchanged across a run (112 → 112); no `.tmp` files or stray `.kv.json` left behind.Task complete and reported.

**Summary:** Added a 25-test `node:test` suite under `test/` that runs `bin/kv.js` as a child process against a per-test temp store file, covering every command, error case and exit code with exact `status`/`stdout`/`stderr` assertions. Added `"test": "node --test test/"` to `package.json` and `.kv.json` to `.gitignore`. `bin/` and `src/` were left untouched.

**Key finding:** On the installed Node v26, `node --test test/` no longer directory-scans — a bare directory is resolved as a module entry point, which failed with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. I bridged it with `test/index.js` importing the four suites, so both `npm test` and `node --test test/` exit 0 (25 pass / 0 fail). The only side effect is that auto-discovery (`node --test` with no args) runs the suite twice; neither acceptance command uses that form.

No CLI bugs surfaced. Temp dirs are cleaned up (count unchanged across a run) and no stray files are left in the repo.

tasks.title: Implement src/store.js storage layer
tasks.spec:
Create `src/store.js` as an ES module with no dependencies, implementing the storage layer exactly as described in the design's 'src/store.js' interface section. Exports: `KEY_PATTERN` (`/^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$/`), `isValidKey(key)`, `StoreError extends Error`, and `Store` with `static async load(filePath)`, `async get(key) -> {found, value?}`, `async set(key, value, { ttlSeconds } = {})`, `async del(key) -> boolean`, `async list() -> string[]`.

Behaviour to implement: the exact JSON file format (object of key -> `{ value: string, expiresAt: number|null }`, pretty-printed with 2-space indent and sorted keys plus trailing newline); a missing file is an empty store while unparseable/non-object/shape-invalid content throws `StoreError` with message `invalid store: <path>`; expiry test `expiresAt !== null && expiresAt <= Date.now()`; `set` writes `expiresAt = ttlSeconds == null ? null : Date.now() + Math.round(ttlSeconds*1000)`; `get`/`del` remove an expired entry and persist before reporting it missing; `list` filters expired keys and sorts ascending without writing; write-through persistence only when the store actually changed; atomic write via a temp file `<basename>.<pid>.<random>.tmp` in the same directory followed by `fs.rename`, with best-effort unlink on failure. Use `node:fs/promises`. Do not validate keys here (the CLI does), do not create missing parent directories, and do not touch any file outside `src/`.

Boundaries: this task owns `src/store.js` only. `bin/kv.js` is written by `kv-cli` against this exact interface, so the exported names and signatures above are frozen. Verify both acceptance commands, which import the module and exercise set/get/list/del, TTL expiry, pruning, the on-disk format and leftover temp files.

""); process.exit(1); }; const s = await Store.load(file); await s.set("a", "one two"); await s.set("b", "x", { ttlSeconds: 0 }); await s.set("c", "y"); const ag = await s.get("a"); if (!ag.found || ag.value !== "one two") fail("get of a live key", ag); const bg = await s.get("b"); if (bg.found) fail("ttl 0 key was still present"); if ((await s.list()).join(",") !== "a,c") fail("list result", await s.list()); if (!(await s.del("c"))) fail("del of an existing key returned false"); if (await s.del("c")) fail("del of a missing key returned true"); const raw = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8")); if (raw.a.value !== "one two" || raw.a.expiresAt !== null || "b" in raw || "c" in raw) fail("on-disk content wrong", raw); const leftovers = fs.readdirSync(dir).filter((n) => n.endsWith(".tmp")); if (leftovers.length) fail("leftover temp files", leftovers); console.log("store module ok");'
acceptance.review: Confirm the store trusts its inputs (no key validation inside Store), that reads which change nothing never rewrite the file, and that the temp file used for atomic writes is created in the same directory as the target so `rename` is atomic.

report.summary: Implemented `src/store.js`, the dependency-free storage layer for the kv CLI, exactly matching the frozen interface in the design. Exports `KEY_PATTERN`, `isValidKey`, `StoreError`, and `Store` with `static async load(filePath)`, `get`, `set`, `del`, and `list`. It parses/validates the JSON store (missing file => empty store; unparseable, non-object, or shape-invalid content throws `StoreError` with message `invalid store: <path>`), reads missing `expiresAt` as null, serializes with sorted keys, 2-space indent and a trailing newline, applies the absolute-millisecond expiry rule, prunes expired entries on `get`/`del` and persists that change, filters (without writing) in `list`, and persists mutations write-through via an atomic temp-file-plus-rename in the target's directory with best-effort unlink on failure. Key validation is left to the CLI and no directories are created.
report.evidence: Both acceptance commands exit 0: the export check printed EXPORTS_OK, and the store exercise printed "store module ok" (set/get/list/del, ttlSeconds:0 expiry, on-disk format with `a` live and `b`/`c` absent, no leftover `.tmp` files). Additional ad-hoc verification passed ("extra checks ok"): missing file loads as empty with no file written; exact serialized bytes for the sorted/pretty/trailing-newline format and `{}` for an empty store; missing `expiresAt` read as null; expired entries pruned and persisted on get/del; `list` left the file bytes untouched; six malformed store contents each rejected with `StoreError` "invalid store: <path>"; key-helper behavior; a `__proto__` key round-tripping safely; no `.tmp` leftovers. A TTL check confirmed a 60s expiry lands ~now+60000ms and stays live ("ttl check ok").
decisions: Internal store data is a null-prototype object so keys such as `__proto__` (allowed by KEY_PATTERN) round-trip as ordinary own properties rather than mutating the prototype; the serialized object is null-prototyped too.
Entry shape validation accepts any extra properties on an entry as long as `value` is a string and `expiresAt` is absent/null/number, rather than rejecting unknown fields.
Atomic writes use `node:crypto` randomBytes for the temp-file suffix and `process.pid`, named `<basename>.<pid>.<random>.tmp` in the target directory.

tasks.title: Implement bin/kv.js CLI entry point
tasks.spec:
Create `bin/kv.js` (ES module, `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang, no dependencies) that imports `Store`, `isValidKey`, `StoreError` from `../src/store.js` and implements the CLI contract described in the design's 'bin/kv.js' section: flag extraction for `--file <path>` and `--ttl <seconds>` anywhere in argv (last occurrence wins, a flag without a following token is a usage error), the first remaining positional token is the command, and no positional token means usage with exit 2.

Commands and exact output: `set <key> <value...>` requires at least one value token, joins the remaining args with single spaces, and writes nothing (exit 0); optional `--ttl` accepts a finite number >= 0 and is stored as `Date.now() + round(seconds*1000)`; `get <key>` prints `value + '
'`; `del <key>` prints `deleted
`; `list` prints non-expired keys sorted ascending joined by `
` with a trailing newline, and prints nothing at all for an empty store. Missing or expired key on get/del: `not found: <key>
` on stderr, exit 1. Key failing `/^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$/` on set/get/del: `invalid key: <key>
` on stderr, exit 1, checked after the argument-count check and before the store is opened. Unknown command, wrong argument count, `--ttl` on get/del/list, invalid `--ttl` value, or a flag missing its value: the exact usage text from the design on stderr, exit 2. Unexpected errors and `StoreError`: `error: <message>
` on stderr, exit 1.

The default store file is `.kv.json` in `process.cwd()`. Use `node:fs/promises`; call `main()` with top-level await and set `process.exitCode` rather than calling `process.exit` after writing output. Boundaries: this task owns `bin/` only; the `src/store.js` interface is frozen by `store-module` and must not be edited. Verify with the four acceptance commands, which spawn the CLI as a child process and check exit codes and exact stdout/stderr for success, overwrite, TTL, missing-key, invalid-key, unknown-command, argument-count and default-`--file` cases.

tasks.title: Add node:test suite and npm test script
tasks.spec:
Add a `node:test` suite under `test/` that drives the CLI as a child process, following the design's 'Testing conventions'. Test files are named `test/*.test.js`; shared helpers go in `test/helpers.js` and must be side-effect free at import time because `node --test test/` loads every `.js` file in the directory. Helpers should create a fresh `fs.mkdtemp` directory per test, spawn `process.execPath` with the absolute path of `bin/kv.js` via `spawnSync(..., { encoding: 'utf8' })`, and expose the child's `status`/`stdout`/`stderr`. Clean up temp directories after each test.

Required coverage, asserting exact `status`, exact `stdout` and exact `stderr`: `set` stores a value and prints nothing; multiple value words are joined with single spaces; overwriting an existing key replaces the value; `get` prints `value + newline`; `get` of a missing key prints `not found: <key>` on stderr and exits 1; `get` of an expired key (write an already-expired absolute `expiresAt` into the store file) prints `not found: <key>`, exits 1, and removes the key from the file; a `--ttl 0` set is expired on the next read (covers the real-clock path without sleeping); `list` prints sorted non-expired keys one per line, excludes expired keys, and prints nothing for an empty store; `del` removes a key, prints `deleted`, exits 0, and prints `not found: <key>` with exit 1 for a missing key; an invalid key (e.g. `bad key`) on set/get/del prints `invalid key: <key>` on stderr and exits 1; an unknown command prints usage on stderr and exits 2; `--file` defaults to `.kv.json` in the child's working directory; the store file is valid JSON matching the documented format and no `.tmp` files are left behind after a write.

Also in this task: add `"scripts": { "test": "node --test test/" }` to `package.json` (keep the existing `name`, `version`, `type`) and add `.kv.json` to `.gitignore`. Boundaries: `test/`, `package.json` and `.gitignore` only; do not change `bin/` or `src/` — if a test reveals a real bug in the CLI, report it instead of editing those files. Acceptance is `npm test` exiting 0.

commands: npm test
node --test test/
acceptance.review: Confirm every command, error case and exit code from the design has at least one test with exact stdout/stderr assertions, that no test depends on wall-clock sleeps or timing margins, and that temp directories are cleaned up so repeated runs are not polluted.

report.summary: Added a node:test suite (25 tests) under test/ that drives bin/kv.js as a child process against a fresh temp store file per test, added the "test" script to package.json, and added .kv.json to .gitignore. Coverage asserts exact status, stdout and stderr for every command, error case and exit code from the design: set (silent, multi-word joining with single spaces, overwrite), get (value + newline), del (deleted / not found), list (sorted, non-expired only, empty store prints nothing), invalid keys on set/get/del (incl. rejected before the store file is touched), unknown command, 13 usage-error cases, missing flag values, --file defaulting to .kv.json in the child cwd, the documented on-disk JSON format, no leftover .tmp files, missing store as empty store, and invalid-store error. TTL is tested with an already-expired absolute expiresAt written into the file (pruned on read) and with --ttl 0, so there are no sleeps or timing margins. Note: on the installed Node v26, `node --test test/` no longer directory-scans (a bare directory is resolved as a module entry point and failed with MODULE_NOT_FOUND), so I added test/index.js that imports the suites; both `npm test` and `node --test test/` then resolve the directory to it and run every suite once.
report.evidence: `npm test` (i.e. `node --test test/`) exits 0 with "tests 25, pass 25, fail 0". `node --test test/` run directly from the project root exits 0 with the same counts. A before/after count of os.tmpdir() kv-* directories was unchanged (112 -> 112) across a run, confirming cleanup; no .tmp files remain after writes (asserted by a test), and no stray .kv.json is created in the repo. git status --short shows only .gitignore and package.json modified and test/ added.
decisions: Node v26 does not directory-scan an argument to --test: `node --test test/` failed with MODULE_NOT_FOUND because a bare directory is resolved as a module entry point. Added test/index.js (imports the four *.test.js suites) so the required invocations resolve the directory to it and run the suites; consequence is that `node --test` with no arguments (auto-discovery) loads both index.js and the suites directly and runs tests twice (49 pass) — the documented/acceptance invocations run them once.

test/helpers.js is side-effect free (pure exports) so it is safe when the runner loads every .js file under test/; each test creates its own fs.mkdtemp dir and registers cleanup with t.after(() => fs.rm(dir, {recursive:true, force:true})).

Expiry is never tested with wall-clock sleeps: tests write an already-expired absolute expiresAt into the store file, or use --ttl 0 (expired immediately because the store treats expiresAt <= Date.now() as expired).
openIssues: Cosmetic only: `node --test` with no arguments (auto-discovery) runs the suite twice because both test/index.js and the individual *.test.js files are discovered; all pass and neither acceptance command uses auto-discovery.

tasks.title: Write README.md documenting the CLI
tasks.spec: Write `README.md` for the `kv` CLI. It must document, accurately and with runnable examples: requirements (Node >= 18, no dependencies) and invocation `node bin/kv.js <command> [args] [--file <path>]`; every command (`set <key> <value...>` with multi-word values and the optional `--ttl <seconds>`, `get`, `del`, `list`) with example invocations and the exact output each prints; the `--file` option and the `.kv.json` default; the exit-code contract (0 success, 1 missing/expired key or invalid key, 2 unknown command or usage error) and the exact messages `not found: <key>`, `invalid key: <key>`; the key pattern `/^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$/`; TTL semantics (absolute millisecond expiry, expired keys disappear on read); the store file format shown as a JSON example; the atomic write behaviour (temp file plus rename, so a killed process never leaves a half-written store); and how to run the tests with `npm test`. Match the behaviour implemented by `kv-cli` and the format in the design document; if the implementation disagrees with the design, report the discrepancy rather than documenting different behaviour. Boundaries: `README.md` only.

projectEvents.summary: Implemented `src/store.js`, the dependency-free storage layer for the kv CLI, exactly matching the frozen interface in the design. Exports `KEY_PATTERN`, `isValidKey`, `StoreError`, and `Store` with `static async load(filePath)`, `get`, `set`, `del`, and `list`. It parses/validates the JSON store (missing file => empty store; unparseable, non-object, or shape-invalid content throws `StoreError` with message `invalid store: <path>`), reads missing `expiresAt` as null, serializes with sorted keys, 2-space indent and a trailing newline, applies the absolute-millisecond expiry rule, prunes expired entries on `get`/`del` and persists that change, filters (without writing) in `list`, and persists mutations write-through via an atomic temp-file-plus-rename in the target's directory with best-effort unlink on failure. Key validation is left to the CLI and no directories are created.

projectEvents.summary: Created bin/kv.js, the CLI entry point for the kv store. It imports Store and isValidKey from ../src/store.js (the frozen store interface, untouched), parses argv with flag extraction for --file and --ttl anywhere in the argument list (last occurrence wins; a flag with no following token is a usage error), treats every other token as positional (so values and keys may begin with dashes), and dispatches set/get/del/list with the exact stdout/stderr text and exit codes from the design. Usage errors exit 2, invalid keys exit 1 after the argument-count check but before the store is opened, and not-found/expired keys exit 1 with `not found: <key>` on stderr. Default store file is `.kv.json` resolved against process.cwd(); results are written with process.stdout/stderr and process.exitCode (no process.exit).

projectEvents.summary: Added a node:test suite (25 tests) under test/ that drives bin/kv.js as a child process against a fresh temp store file per test, added the "test" script to package.json, and added .kv.json to .gitignore. Coverage asserts exact status, stdout and stderr for every command, error case and exit code from the design: set (silent, multi-word joining with single spaces, overwrite), get (value + newline), del (deleted / not found), list (sorted, non-expired only, empty store prints nothing), invalid keys on set/get/del (incl. rejected before the store file is touched), unknown command, 13 usage-error cases, missing flag values, --file defaulting to .kv.json in the child cwd, the documented on-disk JSON format, no leftover .tmp files, missing store as empty store, and invalid-store error. TTL is tested with an already-expired absolute expiresAt written into the file (pruned on read) and with --ttl 0, so there are no sleeps or timing margins. Note: on the installed Node v26, `node --test test/` no longer directory-scans (a bare directory is resolved as a module entry point and failed with MODULE_NOT_FOUND), so I added test/index.js that imports the suites; both `npm test` and `node --test test/` then resolve the directory to it and run every suite once.
